street.description: Hyper-casual Mexican Gen Z — TikTok-native, slang-heavy.

casual_social.description: Default Mexican B2C social — warm, expressive, ¡buena onda!

professional_casual.description: LinkedIn México — professional but recognizably Mexican.

corporate_formal.description: Press, banking, government — neutral Latin American Spanish.

grammar_quirks: Tú (informal you) dominant; usted for formal/elder
'Ahorita' has variable meaning — 'right now' or 'in a bit' depending on context
Use of 'le' for indirect object, even when redundant

code_switching_patterns.english_in_spanish: Spanglish in US-Latino contexts — Texas, California, Florida especially. Common patterns: English nouns in Spanish syntax ('voy al store').
rules: Mexican Gen Z TikTok mixes English freely
Northern Mexico (border states) has more English influence than Central/South

do_not_use: Castilian markers (vosotros, vale, tío) — wrong region
Argentinian voseo (vos, tenés, querés) — wrong region
